concept.title: DITA map structure components

conbody.p: Unlike a book map, which is designed to mirror a traditional printed book with front matter, chapters, appendices, and backmatter, a DITA map is structured as a more flexible, modular container for topics. Its components focus on logical grouping and navigation for web or portal‑style experiences rather than formal print structure.

Typical DITA map structure components include:
Title: the main label for the map (for example, “User Guide” or “API Reference”).
Topic groups <topicgroup>: clusters of related topics (such as “Getting Started”, “Administration”, or “Troubleshooting”) that help organize content without implying a fixed “chapter” boundary.
Topic references <topicref>: links to individual topics, often nested to show a hierarchy (such as concept → task → reference) and reused across multiple maps.
Topic heads <topichead>: navigation labels that group related <topicref> entries (for example, “Getting Started” or “Reference”) without pointing to a physical topic, making the TOC and portal navigation clearer and more modular.
Key definitions <keydef>: reusable keys for topics, products, or phrases that can be referenced via keyref throughout the map.

In short, while a book map emphasizes a fixed, publication‑oriented structure (frontmatter, chapters, backmatter), a DITA map emphasizes modular, topic‑based groupings that can be repurposed across different outputs and user journeys.
